text: REST APIs are a common way to connect different software systems. When you design one, it is important to follow some best practices. First, use clear and meaningful endpoints, such as /users or /orders, so developers can easily understand what each one does. Second, always return the correct status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Third, write good documentation that explains how every endpoint works. Finally, use versioning, for example /v1/users, so that future changes do not break existing applications. Following these simple rules makes your API easier to use and maintain.
